reports.title: Moderna Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Updates

lines: Improves 2026 GAAP operating expense outlook by approximately $0.2 billion from previous estimate
“Building on this momentum, we increased our full-year revenue growth outlook to 15%-25%, while continuing to reduce costs and strengthen our balance sheet.
Revenue: The Company now expects total revenue growth of 15% to 25% in 2026, exceeding its previous outlook of up to 10% growth.
Cost of Sales: Cost of sales for 2026 is expected to be approximately $1.7 billion, including the previously announced $0.9 billion non-recurring litigation settlement charge.

Research and Development Expenses: Research and development expenses for 2026 are expected to be approximately $2.7 billion, reduced from the Company's previous expectation of approximately $2.9 billion.
Selling, General and Administrative Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses for 2026 are expected to be approximately $1.0 billion, unchanged from previous forecast.

desk.headline: Revenue up 29% to $1.3bn, far above estimates, and a surprise profit; 2026 growth outlook raised to 15–25%
results: Revenue rose 29% to $1.31bn, well above the ~$890m expected, mainly on higher COVID vaccine sales abroad under government supply deals.
Moderna turned a $162m profit ($0.38 a share) versus a $200m loss a year ago; analysts had expected a loss of about $1.25 a share.
R&D spending fell 27% to $583m as late-stage infectious disease studies wound down; cost of sales rose 54% with higher volumes.
Cash and investments rose to $8.0bn, helped by $2.6bn net raised from convertible notes, after paying $950m for a litigation settlement.
The flu vaccine mFLUSIVA won US approval, and intismeran (with Merck) had positive Phase 3 melanoma data.

guidance.summary: Moderna now expects 2026 revenue to grow 15–25%, up from up to 10% before, with lower R&D costs and a much higher year-end cash balance of $8.1–8.3bn.

points: CEO Bancel credited newer products and sales in more countries (Canada, the UK, parts of Asia) for the strong quarter.
He said the return to profit came from both stronger sales and lower costs.
The stand-alone flu vaccine will have only a limited US launch this season, as approval came after the contracting cycle.
Bancel said doctors were impressed by the intismeran melanoma data and want to use it in practice.
call.source: CEO interview remarks as reported by Briefs Finance, 6 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Analyst Day on 12 Nov 2026 for longer-term targets.
Regulatory filings for intismeran and pivotal propionic acidemia data.
Collection of the large receivables built up in Q3, which drives the year-end cash figure.
